metadata.explanation: First cut: C(aryl)-N bond formed by SNAr. The target is 4-(morpholin-4-yl)-2-fluorobenzaldehyde; disconnecting the C4-N bond gives 2,4-difluorobenzaldehyde, whose para-fluorine (ortho/para to the CHO activating group) is displaced regioselectively by morpholine, leaving the ortho-F intact. Both partners were confirmed in stock by exact lookup (O=Cc1ccc(F)cc1F, InChIKey WCGPCBACLBHDCI-UHFFFAOYSA-N; C1COCCN1, YNAVUWVOSKDBBP-UHFFFAOYSA-N). validate_disconnection confirmed valid structures, atom-inventory conservation and reaction-class compatibility, but reported no exact dataset reaction/trusted template match (support: none), so confidence is moderate rather than high. Typical conditions: morpholine (1.1-1.5 eq), K2CO3 or Cs2CO3, DMSO/DMF, 60-110 C.

metadata.explanation: Alternative first cut: Pd-catalysed Buchwald-Hartwig C-N coupling. Disconnecting the same C4-N bond but using the aryl bromide synthon gives 4-bromo-2-fluorobenzaldehyde (O=Cc1ccc(Br)cc1F), confirmed in stock by exact lookup (InChIKey UPCARQPLANFGQJ-UHFFFAOYSA-N), plus morpholine (YNAVUWVOSKDBBP-UHFFFAOYSA-N, in stock). Bromide is far more reactive than the retained aryl-F under Pd catalysis, so C-Br amination is chemoselective and the ortho-fluorine survives. validate_disconnection: valid structures, atom inventory conserved, reaction class compatible, but no exact dataset reaction or trusted template matched (support: none) - hence moderate confidence. Practical caveat: the free aldehyde can coordinate/reduce Pd, so protection as an acetal or use of a highly active BrettPhos-type ligand may be needed; dataset support is not experimental proof.
